display_name: The whole Housing and Development Act 1959 under one top-level goal — may the person buy the flat, is the dealing lawful, is the flat safe from creditors, and may the Board re-enter, acquire or penalise instead — and six goals: buying, dealings, the Board's remedies and periods, upgrading, the Board, offences and service
scope: Every provision of the Act as printed in SSO's informal consolidation of the version in force from 15 July 2026 (2020 Revised Edition). Inputs: the Board's and Minister's discretions and opinions, prescribed matters, convictions, the s 63(1)(o) appointed date. Carried as text: the provisions listed in hda-flats.l4 and hda-upgrading-board.l4, and the Schedules. NOT encoded: nothing in the Act.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-09 (tests-independent.l4, 164 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read): 162 pass; the 2 failures (E60, E91) are off-by-one expectations the report itself concedes, kept as expected failures. It found six gaps (ss 50(1)(b), 58(6)-(7), 59(3)(a), 63(1)(m), 63(1)(o), the top-level s 74 penalty), now fixed. The source is SSO's unofficial consolidation. The pipeline has not been run.

forks.F1: s 50(1)(b): a disposal exactly 30 months before the application is barred.
forks.F2: s 62(1)(c): re-entry from day 15 after notice.
forks.F3: ss 50(3A), 59(5A), 66, 68: the Board may act on served + N + 1.
forks.F4: s 63(2): the Minister's higher value, else $250,000.
forks.F5: s 63(1)(o): the appointed date is an input.
forks.F6: s 107: fine or imprisonment, not both.
